context:
Goal: a CI time limit rises with real growth and never turns a run red for time.
Problem (rule): your restart-plan ruling R3 sets limits from measured green runs, but a job that has grown past its limit is cut on every run and never gives a green sample (the restart-plan incident with 11 cuts).
Based on (ruling): R3 item 3: limits come from "measured green runs".
Based on (read): restart-plan section 3.2, the incident where one job was cut 11 times.
Departs from: R3, limits from green runs only — a run cut at its limit also counts, and the limit rises 1.5 times per cut run, up to 360 min.
Meanwhile: the lane builds a as a default that can be switched off.

options.gain: A job that has grown heals in one run.
options.how: Each run cut at its limit raises that job's limit 1.5 times, up to 360 min.
options.label: A cut run counts as a sample (Recommended)
options.lose: A job that truly hangs raises its own limit each cut run (30, 46, 70, 106, 160, 241, 360 min) until the stop on a silent job ends it.

options.how: Keep R3: only green runs set a limit.
options.label: Green runs only, as ruled
options.lose: A grown job stays cut until it passes once at the old limit.

reply: Filed again after your undo: a run cut at its time limit counts as a sample, and the limit rises 1.5 times per cut run up to 360 minutes. Lane time-limits-end-hangs-only builds it.
short: Cut run counts toward the CI time limit?
title: Should a CI run cut at its time limit count as a sample, so the limit can rise?
why: The lane's default rests on it.
